:::{#thm-factorization}
#### Factorization theorem

Let $\pdf\paren{\vx ; \param}$ be the joint probability mass function of a discrete sample $\vX$.
A statistic $\statf{\vX}$ is [sufficient](#def-sufficient) for $\param$
if and only if there are nonnegative functions $\sfac$ and $\rfac$ such that,
for every sample $\vx$ and every $\param$,

$$
\pdf\paren{\vx ; \param} = \sfacf{\statf{\vx}}{\param} \, \rfacf{\vx}
$$ {#eq-factorization}

where $\rfacf{\vx}$ does not depend on $\param$.

Source: @wikipedia_sufficient_statistic.
:::

::: proof

Let $\vx$ be a value of the [sample](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample) $\vX$ and write $t \eqdef \statf{\vx}$.
The event $\vX = \vx$ lies inside the event $\statf{\vX} = t$.

**Sufficient implies a factorization.**
Define $\sfacf{t}{\param} \eqdef \Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t}$
and let $\rfacf{\vx}$ be the conditional probability $\Pr_{\param}\paren{\vX = \vx \given \statf{\vX} = t}$
at any $\param$ with $\Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t} > 0$.
By [sufficiency](#eq-sufficient), $\rfacf{\vx}$ does not depend on which such $\param$ we use.
(If $\Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t} = 0$ for every $\param$, set $\rfacf{\vx} \eqdef 0$.)
Both functions are nonnegative, and at a $\param$ with $\Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t} = 0$
both sides of @eq-factorization are zero, because the event $\vX = \vx$ lies inside the event $\statf{\vX} = t$.
At every other $\param$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pdf\paren{\vx ; \param}
&= \Pr_{\param}\paren{\vX = \vx}
&& \text{(definition of the joint mass function)}\\
&= \Pr_{\param}\paren{\vX = \vx,\ \statf{\vX} = t}
&& \text{(the first event is inside the second)}\\
&= \Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t} \,
   \Pr_{\param}\paren{\vX = \vx \given \statf{\vX} = t}
&& \text{(conditional probability)}\\
&= \sfacf{t}{\param} \, \rfacf{\vx}
&& \text{(definitions of $\sfac$ and $\rfac$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

**A factorization implies sufficient.**
Suppose @eq-factorization holds, and let $t$ be a value with $\Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t} > 0$.
The event $\statf{\vX} = t$ is the union of the disjoint events $\vX = \vy$
over the samples $\vy$ with $\statf{\vy} = t$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t}
&= \sum_{\vy:\, \statf{\vy} = t} \pdf\paren{\vy ; \param}
&& \text{(disjoint events add)}\\
&= \sum_{\vy:\, \statf{\vy} = t} \sfacf{\statf{\vy}}{\param} \, \rfacf{\vy}
&& \text{(factorization)}\\
&= \sum_{\vy:\, \statf{\vy} = t} \sfacf{t}{\param} \, \rfacf{\vy}
&& \text{(each term has $\statf{\vy} = t$)}\\
&= \sfacf{t}{\param} \sum_{\vy:\, \statf{\vy} = t} \rfacf{\vy}
&& \text{(factor out the common term)}
\end{aligned}
$$

This is positive, so $\sfacf{t}{\param} > 0$.
For a sample $\vx$ with $\statf{\vx} = t$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_{\param}\paren{\vX = \vx \given \statf{\vX} = t}
&= \frac{\pdf\paren{\vx ; \param}}{\Pr_{\param}\paren{\statf{\vX} = t}}
&& \text{(conditional probability)}\\
&= \frac{\sfacf{t}{\param} \, \rfacf{\vx}}
        {\sfacf{t}{\param} \sum_{\vy:\, \statf{\vy} = t} \rfacf{\vy}}
&& \text{(factorization, and the display above)}\\
&= \frac{\rfacf{\vx}}{\sum_{\vy:\, \statf{\vy} = t} \rfacf{\vy}}
&& \text{(divide by $\sfacf{t}{\param} > 0$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

which does not depend on $\param$.
For a sample $\vx$ with $\statf{\vx} \neq t$ the conditional probability is zero,
which does not depend on $\param$ either.
So $\statf{\vX}$ is sufficient.

:::
